concerns.text: FR-015 provides a justification for the 15 % equivalence margin but does not reference any user story (e.g., US-3). Without an explicit anchor, this functional requirement is an orphan.
FR-016 explains the choice of effect size d = 0.5 but lacks a traceability link to a user story. It is therefore an orphaned functional requirement.
FR-007 mandates CPU‑only execution but does not explicitly cite a user story (US-2 is the closest). The lack of an explicit anchor makes this requirement an orphan.

FR-003 uses the placeholder **[deferred]** for the discard proportion ("System MUST discard the bottom **[deferred]** of videos ..."). The requirement also mentions a default `filter_discard_percent` of 40 % in the description, creating a contradiction: the discard rate is both undefined (placeholder) and defined (default 40 %). This makes the functional requirement unverifiable.

SC-001 references a target retain/discard rate as **[deferred]** ("The percentage of videos retained after filtering is measured against the target retain rate of **[deferred]** (i.e., discard **[deferred]**)"), but the specification elsewhere (FR-003, Constitution Principle VI) states the intended discard proportion is 40 %. The placeholder leaves the success criterion unmeasurable and inconsistent with the stated design.

FR-009 states that if the retained count is < 64, physics‑preserving augmentation will be applied to reach n ≥ 64, but also says augmented samples are **not** counted toward independent observations, meaning the TOST analysis will still have fewer than the required n ≥ 64 independent samples mandated by FR-006. This creates a methodological inconsistency: the power analysis assumes 64 independent observations per condition, yet the protocol may violate this, undermining the validity of the equivalence test.
